**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear with husks pulled back
- Most kernels are healthy yellow/golden
- Concentrated kernel rot at the **tip/silk end** of the ear
- Affected kernels are brownish-pink/gray, some appear shrunken/collapsed
- Dark material visible around the silk attachment at tip
- A few dark spots scattered on otherwise healthy kernels

**Reasoning:**
- The rot is clearly **starting at the tip** (silk channel end) — this is the hallmark of **Gibberella ear rot**, which infects via the silk channel
- Fusarium rot typically affects scattered/clustered kernels with a white-pink cottony mold and starburst pattern, not a tip-first pattern
- Diplodia starts at the **base** of the ear, not the tip
- Aspergillus produces olive-green powdery spores — not visible here
- The brownish-pink/tan discoloration at the tip with the silk-channel entry point strongly matches Gibberella

The reference collage for Gibberella appeared to show heavily infected/advanced late-season husked material, but the key distinguishing feature is the tip-origin infection via silk, which matches this image.
